Here is a consolidated 12-week program that folds in all adjustments discussed: phase structure, cycle-aware loading, flow/flare-day modifications, cardio progression with a Phase 2 MetCon and Plyometric Day, a Phase 2 HIIT/metabolic conditioning day, a Phases 2–3 plyometric plan, and the option for a Phase 3 1RM testing discussion. It’s written as a week-by-week calendar with clear session order, sets/reps, and notes on tempo, intensity, and special considerations for endometriosis. Dates are anchored to a start date of 2026-06-01. Adjust as needed for actual calendar constraints.

Overview and structure
- Phase 1: Foundations and adaptation (Weeks 1–4)
  - Focus: establish routine, technique, baseline endurance, and pain-management strategies.
  - 4 training days per week plus optional mobility day; 2 cardio sessions; 1 mobility/restorative day.
- Phase 2: Progression with controlled intensity (Weeks 5–8)
  - Focus: progressive resistance loading; cardio progression with a push in intensity; MetCon day; Plyometric day; careful flare-window planning.
  - 4 training days per week; 4 cardio days (including HIIT/MetCon day); 1 plyometric day; 1 optional recovery day.
- Phase 3: Stability, conditioning, and preparation for potential 1RM testing (Weeks 9–12)
  - Focus: consolidate gains, higher quality conditioning, maintain cycle-aware adjustments; option for a submaximal testing protocol if desired; continue 4 training days and cardio as tolerated; plyometrics reduced frequency if symptoms arise.
  - 4 training days per week; 4 cardio days (with flexibility in MetCon/HIIT integration); plyometrics as scheduled; optional 1RM discussion post-testing if chosen.

Important safety notes that apply throughout
- Flow/flare days: no HIIT/MetCon or high-impact plyometrics; emphasize low-impact cardio, mobility, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor activation as advised.
- Valsalva caution: avoid breath-holding during lifts; cue bracing with diaphragmatic breathing rather than a strenuous Valsalva; exhale on exertion.
- Pain monitoring: track pain, cramping, bowel/bladder symptoms, sleep, and fatigue. If symptoms intensify, dial back intensity, volume, and adjust via a deload or recovery week.
- Medical clearance: ensure clinician approval for cycle-phase testing, MetCon/HIIT during certain windows, and any testing (1RM or RM) adjustments.
- Nutrition and recovery: follow the anti-inflammatory plan; ensure post-workout protein and carbs within 1–2 hours; hydration; sleep 7–9 hours; stress management.

Week-by-week program (start 2026-06-01)

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 – Foundation and adaptation

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07)
- Resistance Day A (Lower/Full-Body) – 45–55 min
  - Warm-up: 5–7 min light cardio + hip/ankle mobility
  - Goblet squat or chair-assisted squat: 3x10 (tempo 2-0-2)
  - Romanian deadlift to deadlift assist (dumbbell/kettlebell): 3x10
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust: 3x12
  - Standing single-leg balance + hip abduction: 2x12 per leg
  - Pallof press or anti-rotation hold: 3x12
  - Cool-down: 5–7 min mobility, diaphragmatic breathing 2x1 min
- Resistance Day B (Upper/Push-Pull) – 40–50 min
  - Warm-up: 5–7 min light cardio + shoulder mobility
  - Dumbbell bench/floor press: 3x10
  - Seated row or band row: 3x12
  - Dumbbell shoulder press (neutral grip): 3x10
  - Lat pulldown or band pull-aparts: 3x12
  - Plank hold: 3x20–30 sec
  - Side planks: 2x15–20 sec per side
- Cardio (2 sessions): 1x 20–30 min at easy pace; 1x 10–15 min light swim or 15–20 min easy bike
- Mobility/Recovery: 10–15 min daily focus

Week 2
- A: Lower/Full-Body – 4x10 main lifts; 3x12 core/anti-rotation
- B: Upper – 3x12 rows; 3x10 presses; 3x12 pulls
- Cardio: 25–35 min easy; 1 interval day (1 min on/2 min off, RPE ~4–5)
- Mobility: 12–15 min; add thoracic extensions

Week 3
- A: Lower – add tempo work 3x8 goblet squat tempo 3-0-2; hip circles activation
- B: Upper – incline variations if comfortable
- Cardio: 2x per week 25–40 min steady; 1 very light interval (2 cycles of 60s work/120s rest)
- Focus: technique, breath, avoid heavy Valsalva

Week 4 – Deload
- A: 2–3 sets of main lifts at ~60% load
- B: 2–3 sets lighter with focus on form
- Cardio: 1 longer easy session 30–40 min; 1 short recovery tempo 15–20 min
- Mobility/Recovery: 15–20 min daily

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 – Progression with cardio push, MetCon and Plyo

Week 5 – Baseline cardio build + MetCon introduction
- Resistance Day A (Lower): 3x12 goblet squats; 3x10 RDL; 3x12 hip thrust; 2x12 walking lunges
- Resistance Day B (Upper): 3x12 DB bench; 3x12 one-arm row; 3x12 overhead press (neutral); 2x15 band pull-aparts
- Core: Pallof press 3x12; dead bugs 3x12
- Cardio (4 days): 
  - Day A: Walk 30–40 min; 4x1 min brisk segments (RPE 5) with 2 min easy
  - Day B: Bike 30 min steady
  - Day C: Swim 25–30 min steady or 4x2 min easy intervals
  - Day D: Optional easy walk 20–25 min
- Plyometric Day (Week 5): see Plyometric Day content in Week 5–8 plan (low volume)
- MetCon Day (Phase 2): 12–20 min total, 20–30s work, 60–90s rest on cycling/elliptical; 6 rounds; warm-up 5–10 min

Week 6
- Resistance Day A: 4x10 goblet squat; 3x10 RDL; 3x12 hip thrust; 2x12 balance work
- Resistance Day B: 4x10 DB bench; 4x10 row; 3x12 lateral raise; 3x12 band pull-aparts
- Core: Pallof press 3x12; dead bug to reach 3x12
- Cardio:
  - Day A: Walk 35–45 min with 3x2 min faster pace
  - Day B: Bike 30–35 min with 1–2 min higher effort mid-session (RPE 6)
  - Day C: Swim 30 min; 4x2 min intervals
  - Day D: Elliptical 25–30 min with 5x30–45s bursts (RPE 6) and 60–90s easy
- Flare window planning: if near 2026-07-10 to 13, scale back

Week 7
- Resistance Day A: 4x8–10 squats; 3x8 RDL; 3x12 hip thrust; 2x12 split squats
- Resistance Day B: 4x8–10 DB bench; 4x8–10 row; 3x12 push-ups (knee) or incline; 3x12 face pull
- Core: Pallof press 3x12; oblique curls 3x12
- Cardio: 
  - Day A: Walk 40–50 min with 1.5–2 min brisk segments
  - Day B: Bike 35–40 min with 5 min tempo (RPE 6–7)
  - Day C: Swim 30–35 min; 6×1 min faster with 1 min easy
  - Day D: Recovery cardio 20–25 min easy
- MetCon Day: opt to continue once weekly if tolerable
- Plyometric Day: as scheduled in Phase 2 plan Week 5–8

Week 8 – Phase 2 taper/transition
- Resistance Day A: 3x10 squats; 3x10 RDL; 2x12 hip thrust
- Resistance Day B: 3x10 bench; 3x10 row; 2x12 lateral raise
- Core: Pallof press 2x12; plank variations 2x12
- Cardio: 
  - Day A: Walk 30–40 min
  - Day B: Bike 25–30 min steady
  - Day C: Swim 25–30 min comfortable pace
  - Day D: Light cardio/mobility 20–25 min
- Plyometric Day: optional, low volume
- MetCon Day: optional or replaced with mobility/low-intensity cardio if symptoms

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 – Stability, conditioning, and testing preparation

Week 9
- Resistance Day A: Full-body pattern 3–4x8–10; ensure control
- Resistance Day B: 4x8–10 bench; 4x8–10 row; 3x12 overhead press; 2x12 band pull-aparts
- Core: 3x12 Pallof press; 3x12 dead bugs
- Cardio:
  - Day A: 30–40 min steady; 1–2 min brisk segments if energy allows
  - Day B: 25–35 min steady
  - Day C: 30–40 min swim
- Mobility: 15–20 min; breathing work 5 min
- Plyometric Day: as per Week 5–8 plan, reassess readiness

Week 10
- Resistance Day A: 4x8 squats; 4x8 RDL; 3x12 hip thrust; 2x12 step-ups
- Resistance Day B: 4x8–10 DB press; 4x8–10 row; 3x12 face pull; 2x12 planks
- Core: 3x12 Pallof press; 3x12 chop variations
- Cardio: 2x 25–35 min steady
- Recovery: 20–25 min gentle yoga or mobility

Week 11
- Resistance Day A: 4x6–8 squats; 4x6–8 RDL; 3x12 hip thrust; 2x12 unilateral work
- Resistance Day B: 4x6–8 DB bench; 4x6–8 row; 3x12 overhead press; 2x12 band pull-aparts
- Core: 3x12 Pallof press; 3x12 dead bug to side reach
- Cardio:
  - Day A: 30–40 min steady
  - Day B: 15–20 min light intervals
  - Day C: 30–40 min steady
  - Day D: 20–25 min mobility or light cardio
- Flare window awareness: keep intensity moderate around 2026-08-04 to 07; scale back if needed
- MetCon/Plyo: maintain or scale back based on symptoms

Week 12 – Finisher and maintenance
- Resistance Day A: 3x10 compound lifts; 2x12 accessories
- Resistance Day B: 3x10 DB bench; 3x10 row; 2x12 lateral raises
- Core work: 2–3 sets of anti-rotation and planks
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions of 25–30 min easy; 1 longer 40–45 min easy if energy allows
- Mobility/Recovery: 20–25 min; breathing and relaxation
- Testing/Next steps: plan for progression and maintenance; if desired, schedule a 1RM or RM test after a clinician-approved window (see testing notes below)

Testing options at end of Phase 3 (optional)
- 1RM testing: Only if medically cleared, symptoms controlled, and client comfortable; follow safe protocol (see below).
- Submax RM testing: 3RM or 5RM tests to estimate 1RM; velocity-based estimates if equipment available.
- Testing lifts: choose a small set of primary lifts aligned with your program (e.g., back squat or goblet squat; hip hinge/deadlift; bench or DB press; overhead press).
- 1RM testing protocol safeguards:
  - Pre-test: confirm no new symptoms; hydration; warm-up with ramping sets; pain-free technique
  - Attempt progression: 3–5 attempts with 2–4 minutes rest
  - Breathing: diaphragmatic breathing; avoid Valsalva; exhale on exertion
  - Stop rules: if pain, significant cramping, or technique degradation
  - Post-test: cooldown, hydration, nutrition; plan for de-load if needed

Nutrition and recovery integration
- Maintain anti-inflammatory nutrition as earlier plan outlined; ensure post-workout protein/carb intake on resistance and cardio days; emphasize hydration and sleep
- Supplements as advised by clinician (omega-3s, vitamin D, magnesium, probiotics) and adjust based on symptoms
- Symptom tracking during training; adjust fueling around cycle phases and near flare windows

Delivery and implementation options
- If you want, I can produce:
  - A clean, calendar-ready 12-week template with day-by-day sessions, exact sets/reps, tempo, and RPE targets, including MetCon, Plyometric, and the HIIT/MetCon day
  - A printable weekly tracker for workouts, nutrition, symptoms, and cycle awareness
  - A cycle-aware calendar with color-coding for intensity, flare windows, and recovery days
  - A dedicated testing protocol and templates for documenting results and updating loads
- To tailor precisely, provide:
  - Your client’s equipment inventory (free weights, machines, box height, kettle bells, pool access)
  - Any preferred modalities (e.g., no swimming, but cycling allowed)
  - Approximate 1RM lifting history or current submax loads
  - Clinician guidance or any contraindications for maximal efforts or plyometrics

If you’d like, I can deliver the final version as a ready-to-use week-by-week PDF or spreadsheet, with:
- Day names aligned to your schedule
- Exact exercise selections per day
- Reps/sets/rests
- Intensity targets (RPE, tempo)
- Flare-day rules clearly annotated
- MetCon and Plyo days clearly scheduled
- 1RM testing plan (optional) with pre/post-checks

Tell me your equipment specifics, any lifts you want prioritized for testing, and whether you want the 1RM option included in Phase 3. I’ll turn this into a fully fleshed, calendar-ready plan.
